annotations.title: This vvaſt.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Coſt beſtowed vpon Chriſtes body then aliue, being to the ſame not neceſſary, ſeemed to the diſciples loſt and fruitles: ſo the like beſtowed vpon the ſame body in the Sacrament, vpon altars, or Churches, ſeemeth to the ſimple loſt, or leſſe meritorious, then if the ſame were beſtowed vpon the poore.

annotations.title: Good worke.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Coſt beſtowed for religion, deuotion, and ſignification, is a meritorious worke, and often more meritorious then to geue to the poore, though both be very good, and in ſome caſe the poore are to be preferred: yea <mn>[2]</mn> in certaine caſes of neceſſity, the Church wil breake the very conſecrated veſſels and iewels of ſiluer and gold, aud beſtow them in workes of mercy. But we may remember very wel, and our fathers knew it much better, that the poore were then beſt releeued, when moſt was beſtowed vpon the Church.

annotations.title: Haue not.
annotations.text: ◦ We haue him not in viſible maner as he conuerſed on the earth with his diſciples, needing releefe like other poore men: but we haue him after an other ſort in the B. Sacrament, and yet haue him truly and really the ſelf ſame body. Therfore he ſaith, they ſhould not haue him, becauſe they ſhould not ſo haue him, but after an other maner. as when he ſaid Luc. 24 as though he were not then with them, When I was with you.

notes.text: Christ alwaies with vs in the B. Sacrament.

annotations.title: Twelue.
annotations.text: ◦ It muſt needes be a great myſterie that he was to worke in the inſtitution of the new Sacrifice by the maruelous tranſmutation of bread and wine into his body and bloud. Whereas he admitted none (although many preſent in the citie) but the twelue Apoſtles, which were already taught to beleue it without contradiction Io. 6, and were to haue the adminiſtration and conſecration thereof by the Order of Prieſthod, which alſo was there geuen them to that purpoſe. Whereas at the eating of the Paſchal lambe al the familie was wont to be preſent.

notes.text: A wonderful mysterie in the institution of the B. Sacrament.

annotations.title: He tooke bread.
annotations.text: Here at once is inſtituted, for the continuance of the external office of Chriſtes eternal Prieſthod according to the order of Melchiſedec, [1] both a Sacrifice and a Sacrament, though the Scriptures geue neither of theſe names to this action: and our Aduerſaries without al reaſon or religion accept in a ſort the one, and vtterly deny the other. A Sacrifice, in that it is ordeined to continew the memory of Chriſtes death and oblation vpon the Croſſe, and the application of the general vertue thereof to our particular neceſſities, by conſecrating the ſeueral elements, not into Chriſtes whole perſon as it was borne of the virgin or now is in heauen, but the bread into his body apart, as betrayed, broken, and geuen for vs: the wine into his bloud apart, as ſhed out of his body for remiſſion of ſinnes and dedication of the new Teſtament, which be conditions of his perſon as he was in ſacrifice and oblation. In which myſtical and vnſpeakable maner, he would haue the Church to offer and ſacrifice him daily, and he in myſterie and Sacrament dyeth, though now not only in heauen, but alſo in the Sacrament, he be in deede per Concomitantiam (as the Church calleth it, that is, by ſequele of al his partes to ech other) whole, aliue, and immortal. Which point becauſe our Aduerſaries vnderſtand not, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God, [2]they blaſpheme, and abuſe the people to their damnation. It is alſo a Sacrament, in that it is ordeined to be receiued into our bodies and to feede the ſame to reſurrection and immortality, and to geue grace and ſaluation to our ſoules, if we worthely receiue it.

notes.text: The holy Eucharist is both a Sacrifice and a Sacrament.

annotations.title: Bleſſed.
annotations.text: [1] Our Aduerſaries for the two words that are in Greeke and Latin, benedixit, and, gratias egit, he bleſſed, he gaue thanks, vſe only the later, of purpoſe to ſignifie that Chriſt bleſſed not nor conſecrated the bread and the wine, and ſo by that bleſſing wrought any effect vpon them, but gaue thanks only to his Father, as we do in ſaying grace. But the truth is that the word εὐλογεῖν, ſignifieth properly to bleſſe, and is referred to the thing that is bleſſed, as Luc. 9 of the fiſhes, εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς, benedixit eis, he bleſſed them, and thereby wrought in them that wonderful multiplication. So the bleſſing of God is always effectual: and therefore here alſo he bleſſed the bread, and by that bleſſing, with the words folowing, made it his body [2]. Ambroſ. li. de his qui initi. myſt. c. 9. Aug. ep. 59. ad Paulinum. Now whereas taking the cuppe it is ſaid, he gaue thanks. We ſay that it is all one with bleſſing, and that he bleſſed the cuppe, as before the bread: as it is euident by theſe words of S. Paul [3], Calix cui benedicimus, the cuppe which we bleſſe: and therefore he calleth it, Calicem benedictionis, the cuppe of bleſſing, vſing the ſame Greeke word that is ſpoken of the bread. But why is it then ſaid here, he gaue thanks? Becauſe we tranſlate the words faithfully as in the Greeke and the Latin, and becauſe the ſenſe is all one, as we are taught by S. Paul before alleged, and by the Fathers, which call this geuing of thanks ouer the cuppe or ouer the bread, the bleſſing thereof. S. Juſtin. in fin. 2. Apol. Panem Euchariſtiſatum: [4] S. Irenee li. 4. c. 34. Panem in quo gratiæ actæ ſunt. S. Cyprian de coen. Do. Calix ſolenni benedictione ſacratus. that is, The bread bleſſed by giving thanks vpon it, The cuppe conſecrated by ſolemne bleſsing.

notes.text: The blessing of Christ referred to the creatures and working an effect in them.

annotations.title: This is.
annotations.text: ◦ The bread and the wine be turned into the body and bloud of Chriſt by the ſame omnipotent power by which the world was made, and the Word was incarnate in the wombe of the virgin. Damaſc. li. 4 c. 14. Cypr. de Cœn. Domini. Amb. li. de myſt. init. c. 9.

annotations.title: My body.
annotations.text: ◦ He ſaid not, This bread is a figure of my body: or, This wine is a figure of my bloud: but, This is my body, and, This is my bloud. Damaſc. li. 4 c. 14. Theophyl. in hunc locum. Conc. 2. Nic. act. 6, to. 4 eiuſdem actionis in fine. When ſome fathers cal it a figure or ſigne, they meane the outward formes of bread and wine.

notes.text: No figuratiue but a real presence.

annotations.title: Bloud of the new Teſtament.
annotations.text: As the old Teſtament was dedicated with bloud in theſe wordes, This is the bloud of the Teſtament &c. Heb. 9. ſo here is the inſtitution of the new Teſtament in Chriſtes bloud, by theſe wordes, This is the bloud of the new Teſtament &c. ◦ Which is here myſtically ſhed, and not only afterward vpon the Croſſe: for the Greeke is the preſent tenſe in al the Euangeliſtes, and S. Paul: and likewiſe ſpeaking of the body 1 Cor. 11. it is in the Greeke the preſent tenſe, and Luc. 22. and in the Latin here. And the Heretikes them ſelues ſo put it in their tranſlations.

annotations.title: Fruite of the vine.
annotations.text: [1] S. Luke putteth theſe wordes before he come to the conſecration, whereby it ſeemeth that he ſpeaketh of the wine of the Paſchal lambe, and therfore nameth it, the fruite of the vine. but if he ſpeake of the wine which was now his bloud, he nameth it notwithſtanding wine, as S. Paule nameth the other bread, for three cauſes: firſt becauſe it was ſo before: as Eue is called Adams bone, [2]and, Aarons rod deuoured their roddes: [3]Whereas they were not now roddes, but ſerpents. And, He taſted the water turned into wine: [4]Whereas it was now wine and not water: and ſuch like. ſecondly, becauſe it keepeth the formes of bread and wine, and things are called as they appeare: as when Raphael is called a yong man Tob. 5. and, Three men appeared to Abraham Gen. 18. Whereas they were three Angels. thirdly, becauſe Chriſt in this Sacrament is very true and principal bread and wine, feeding and refreſhing vs in body and ſoule to euerlaſting life.

notes.text: The elements after consecration called bread and wine.

annotations.title: Not as I wil.
annotations.text: A perfect example of obedience and ſubmitting our ſelf and our willes to Gods will and ordinance in al aduerſity: and that we ſhould deſire nothing temporal, but vnder the condition of his holy pleaſure and appointment.

annotations.title: Watch and pray.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Hereof came Vigils and Nocturnes, that is, watching and praying in the night, commonly vſed in the Primitiue Church of al Chriſtians, as is plaine by S. Cyprian <mn>[2]</mn> and <mn>[3]</mn> S. Hierom: but afterward and vntil this day, ſpecially of Religious perſons.

notes.text: De orat. Do. nu. 15. * Adu. Vigilant. ep. 53.

annotations.title: Wench.
annotations.text: ◦ S. Gregorie declaring the difference of the Apoſtles before the receiuing of the Holy Ghoſt and after, ſaith thus: Euen this very Paſtor of the Church him ſelf, at whoſe moſt ſacred body we ſitte, how weake he was, the wenche can tell you: but how ſtrong he was after, his anſwer to the high Prieſt declareth, Act. 5, 29: We muſt obey God rather then men. Greg. ho. 20 io Euang.

notes.text: The vertue of the holy Ghost.

annotations.title: To curſe.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> A goodly example and warning to mans infirmity, and to take heede of preſumption, and to hang only vpon God in tentations.

annotations.title: Wept bitterly.
annotations.text: ◦ S. Ambroſe in his Hymne that the Church vſeth at Laudes, ſpeaking of this, ſaith, Hoc ipſa Petra eccleſiæ canente, culpam diluit. When the Cocke crewe, the Rocke of the Church him ſelf waſhed away his fault. S. Auguſt. 1 Retract. c. 21.
